There are three areas that can cause problems for cycling a AR-15

First remove the bolt (easy to do) Manually operate the bolt carrier with the charging handle very slowly. The movement of the bolt carrier should be smooth. If the Gas tube is misaligned the bolt carrier will not go all the way forward when slowly eased forward.

Secondly don't worry about lines on the brass at this point. The round being stripped out of the magazine will cause lines on the brass. The magazine lips ride on the case.

If the movement of the bolt carrier is smooth and you can't see/feel any binding then the problem is with the bolt or the chamber. Order some go/no go head spacing gauges. If the bolt closes on a no go gauge then you have excessive head space and the high pressure of the round will cause the neck to expand and bind in the throat area of the chamber. (This is probably what is happening) If you don't want to buy go/no go head spacing gauges then use machinists blueing in the chamber. Apply the bluing with a paint brush all the way down the chamber and into the neck and the throat.. When you camber a round and lock up the bolt the machinists bluing will transfer to the case of the round. You should see a even coat of bluing on the round when it is extracted.

Also get some machinists blueing and liberally coat the locking lugs in the chamber of the barrel. When the bolt locks up you should see a even transfer of the bluing from the locking lugs of the barrel to the lugs on the bolt.

MACHINISTS BLUEING IS REALLY GOOD STUFF AND YOU CAN USE DIAGNOSE A LOT OF PROBLEMS.
